name: pcalc
desc: Calculator for those working with multiple bases, sizes, and close to the bits
why: A programmer's calculator for bit-level work across bases and sizes; niche and close to the metal, but mostly a calculator.

brief.what_it_is: pcalc is a terminal calculator for programmers that shows binary, hexadecimal and decimal representations of a number at the same time. You type expressions such as 0xff + 0b101101 - 5 or 2+2*3, and it displays the result in all three bases. It also offers bitwise operators (AND, OR, NOR, XOR, NOT, shifts, rotates, two's complement, and byte-order swap) and lets you choose the operand width, from 1 to 64 bits. It is built with ncurses and runs in a terminal.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the idea came while its author was developing a Nintendo Game Boy emulator, where the online tools they found were clunky and did not allow "nice multitasking". The stated goal is a calculator that gives programmers maximum efficiency and flexibility when working with multiple bases, bitwise operations, and various operand sizes.
brief.how_it_works: Input is parsed as an inline expression with operator precedence and parentheses, and numbers can be written in decimal, 0x hex, or 0b binary. Arithmetic runs at 64 bits by default, and typing a width such as 16bit or 8bit switches the operand size; the displayed number is unsigned. Single-character operators map to operations, and the interface panels (history, binary, hex, decimal, operation) can be toggled by typing their names or set at launch with command-line flags.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew and AUR installs need nothing extra. Building from source needs gcc, ncurses, and the source files; the README says to install ncurses first with your system's package manager and gives the Debian/Ubuntu package names. The source install goes to /usr/local/bin via sudo make install. No account, runtime, or config file is mentioned. The only optional setup is a shell alias to pick a default interface, and the --colors flag enables color output.
brief.standout: Most calculators show one base at a time, but pcalc keeps hex, binary and decimal visible together and lets you switch the bit width inline. Its operator set includes rotate, NOR, and a byte-order swap (SE, using the current bit width), which are rare in everyday calculators and fit low-level work like emulator development.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no release dates, changelog, or maintenance note that I could see. It references a v2.0 screenshot and is packaged in Homebrew and the AUR, which suggests it has been maintained at least into the packaging stage, but I could not confirm recent commits.
brief.caveats: Terminal only, with no GUI. Color output depends on the terminal's color profile. Values are displayed unsigned, and the operand size defaults to 64 bits. Building from source requires ncurses and a C toolchain. The README gives no license, though it describes the project as open source. The README does not list platforms beyond Homebrew, Arch-based distros and Debian-style source builds.
